evidence: Cic. Or. 50: alia prīma pōnet, alia postrēma (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: For the last time is postrēmum: hodiē postrēmum mē vidēs, you are seeing me for the last time today (Ter. And. 2.1.22, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Caes. BG 5.56: quī ex iīs novissimus venit (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 87: Cicero spoke last, Cicerō novissimus locūtus est
terms.comment: Varro says that in his youth some old men still avoided it as too new a word (Varr. LL 6.59, Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: the itch take the last one! (last one there’s a rotten egg)

phrases.latin: prīmus cubitū surgat, postrēmus cubitum eat
phrases.english: let him be the first to get up and the last to go to bed

phrases.latin: prīnceps in proelium ībat, ultimus cōnsertō proeliō excēdēbat
phrases.english: he was the first to go into battle and the last to leave it once it was joined

sources: Lewis & Short: postremus · Lewis & Short: ultimus · Lewis & Short: extremus · Lewis & Short: novissimus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 87, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
